evidence.note: probe counted changes.changed_paths reads during L.scan over 3 merged items: 18 reads unfixed (6/item), 3 after the per-scan cache (1/item). Claim CONFIRMED: verdict re-derived changed_paths on every probe; cache asks git once per item.
rules pack read from the claim brief: r-task-phase-needs-wave, r-gemini-key-load (export GEMINI_API_KEY before review), r-derived-cache-bounded (RepoFacts derives memory per scan, nothing written).

changed_paths/_read/_default_branch memoize via a per-scan cache dict threaded from recovery.scan -> _note_landed -> verdict -> changed_paths/readme_report/observed_globs (read=lambda _r,_i: own). Regression test test_recover_scan_cache.py fails on unfixed (18 reads vs 3) and passes fixed (3).

chunk_findings.detail: The regression counter wraps `ddflow.services.changes.changed_paths`, but the scan path this bug names is `CM.verdict`, and the change puts the shared cache on `ddflow/services/completion/_changed.py`'s `changed_paths`. With T1–T3 merged and lapsed, an unfixed verdict can still re-diff each item on every probe (~5 git derivations per item) while `derived` stays empty, so `len(derived) <= len(items)` passes. The bound also accepts zero calls, so the test is green whenever the hot path does not go through the patched symbol.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_recover_scan_cache.py:test_a_scan_derives_each_merged_items_diff_once

chunk_findings.detail: The regression still monkeypatches `ddflow.services.changes.changed_paths` (`CH.changed_paths`) and counts only that name. The bug and the scan path under test are `CM.verdict` / `ddflow/services/completion/_changed.py`'s `changed_paths`, which recovery now calls with a shared `cache` (`L.scan` → `_note_landed` → `CM.verdict(..., cache=cache)`). A function already bound by `from ddflow.services.changes import changed_paths` is not replaced by `setattr(CH, "changed_paths", counting)`, so with T1–T3 merged and lapsed an unfixed verdict can still re-diff each item on every probe while `derived` stays empty. `len(derived) == len(items)` then fails on both the unfixed and the fixed code (false red), or never sees the ~5 git derivations per item if those calls never go through the patched attribute. The bound change only stops a vacuous `<=` pass; it does not wrap the hot path.
